learning_outcomes.text: Applies the principles of thermal engineering correctly.
Becomes aware of the environmental problems generated by refrigerants.
Applies quality criteria in the selection and operation of industrial refrigeration systems.
Understands the operation of a mechanical vapor compression refrigeration cycle and the effect of operating conditions on the performance of a refrigeration cycle.
Solves problems related to air conditioning processes.

syllabus_topics: 1. Introduction: Applications and refrigeration methods. Property diagram of pure substances. Energy balance in open systems. The second law of thermodynamics and the Carnot cycle.
2. Refrigerants: Primary and secondary refrigerants. Nomenclature and classification. Refrigerant mixtures. Effect of refrigerants on the environment: climate change and ozone layer depletion.

3. The mechanical vapor compression refrigeration cycle: Main elements. Operating principle. The P-h diagram. The ideal single-stage compression cycle. The real compression cycle. Volumetric behavior. Multi-stage compression cycles.
4. Compressors: Function and classification. Reciprocating compressors. Rotary volumetric compressors. Centrifugal compressors. Capacity control.
5. Condensers: Air condensers. Water condensers. Evaporative condensers.
6. Evaporators: Dry and flooded evaporators. Direct and indirect expansion evaporators. Ice formation control.
7. Expansion devices: Function. Capillary tubes. Thermostatic valves. Electronic valves.
8. Psychrometry: Humid air as an ideal gas. Humid air variables. The psychrometric diagram. Typical processes in air conditioning.
teaching_methods: Problem/exercise solving in the ordinary classroom
assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 3/10 is required for each continuous assessment test. The second call exam will cover all course material and will have a weight of 100%. During evaluative tests, mobile phones, tablets, and other unauthorized electronic devices must be turned off and out of sight. Fraudulent use of AI in evaluative tests is prohibited. Fraudulent completion of any evaluative activity will result in a failing grade for that activity, and depending on the severity, may lead to disciplinary action.
